purpose: Permanent adversarial cases derived from project history. These fixtures specify distinctions future rules and migrations must preserve; they are not new historical evidence.

fixtures.name: Artigas provenance and fabrication separation
must_preserve: San Jose de Mayo predecessor history and Montevideo exact-object fabrication statements must not be silently reconciled.
A later Smithsonian inventory statement does not become an independent contemporary root merely because Smithsonian is institutionally authoritative.
Commission/authorship, model execution, fabrication and bronze casting are distinct propositions when evidence distinguishes them.
Unknown caster or foundry remains unknown rather than being inferred from sculptor/model attribution.
Source-root uncertainty must remain visible until upstream records are retrieved.
failure_signals: conflicting place/fabrication claims collapse into one normalized fact
institution count substitutes for claim-level independence
CREATED_BY absorbs casting/fabrication roles without evidence

fixtures.name: San Martin attribution and inheritance
must_preserve: Daumas and Dumont attributions remain a documented conflict until source genealogy/evidence resolves it.
U.S. statutory text is direct evidence for legal acceptance or statutory description, not automatically expert art-historical proof of authorship.
An Argentine government republication and Revista Legado do not receive independent-lineage credit when one explicitly derives from the other.
The underlying Revista Legado citations remain a research target rather than being inferred from the downstream republication.
failure_signals: one disputed name is normalized away
government authority is treated as universal authority fit
downstream republication is counted as independent corroboration

fixtures.name: Cuban Friendship Urn asymmetric provenance
must_preserve: Government/Republic of Cuba and citizens-of-Cuba donor formulations remain source-specific until their origins are traced.
Legal acceptance, financing/donation, presentation, receipt, installation and custody are distinct propositions.
An inscription on the physical object is distinct from an NPS transcription of that inscription; the latter is an access/transcription witness unless independently probative.
Material-from-Maine provenance requires evidence addressing material lineage, not merely ceremony or object identity.
Unequal survival/accessibility of U.S. and Cuban records does not itself establish greater historical truthfulness of the surviving U.S. lane.
A bounded unsuccessful Cuban archive search is an archival gap, not negative historical evidence.
failure_signals: legal acceptance is used as proof of donor identity or financing
transcription and physical inscription are counted as independent sources
missing Cuban records are treated as disconfirmation
